validityExplanation: The report contains a completed correctness verdict and two specific conditional findings. The wrapper overmatched the word pending in the final semantic-check clause, producing exit4; preserve that receipt and original validity record. This is a completed review with its two requested semantic checks resolved below, not an initialization placeholder.

finding.body: In write-journal-core.ts undoLastWrites, the previous assertSandboxPath({filePath, cwd: targetRoot, root: targetRoot}) check is replaced by assertNoPathAliasEscape({absolutePath: entry.absPath, rootPath: targetRoot}). If assertNoPathAliasEscape does not perform the same containment/alias validation (e.g., it only rejects path-alias tokens and does not verify the target is inside rootRoot), undo could restore journal snapshot bytes to a target outside the sandbox/workspace, turning a containment check into a weaker one. Need to confirm the exact semantics of assertNoPathAliasEscape vs assertSandboxPath before this is considered safe.
finding.title: Undo target validation may be weaker after swapping assertSandboxPath for assertNoPathAliasEscape

decisions.reason: Undo first checks lexical containment via toRelativeWorkspacePathFromResolved(targetRoot, entry.absPath), then calls assertNoPathAliasEscape and performs rooted fs-safe restoration. The previous assertSandboxPath performs resolveSandboxPath containment then calls exactly the same assertNoPathAliasEscape helper. Both alias-policy options were undefined in the old call and remain at their default in the new call. The new arrangement preserves containment and alias checks while avoiding a second raw-input expansion of the stored filename.

finding.body: In wrapToolWithWriteJournal, paths for non-apply_patch tools are now resolved via resolveWorkspaceFile before acquirePatchBatchLocks, and the previous lockTargets mapping (path.isAbsolute ? path.resolve : path.resolve(workspaceRoot, filePath)) is replaced by the already-resolved paths. If resolveWorkspaceFile (now resolveToCwd) resolves inputs differently than the native write/edit tool's own resolver for some input form (e.g., a raw absolute path containing a literal ~ directory, or an @-prefixed path), the journal lease target and the actual written target can diverge, so the lock would not serialize writes to the same file. The new tests cover @ and file-URL forms, but the equivalence with the native resolver for all accepted input forms needs verification.
finding.title: Journal lock target may diverge from the native write target for some input forms

decisions.reason: Native write.ts and edit.ts both import resolveToCwd from sessions/tools/path-utils.js and call it on the original path and cwd. resolveWorkspaceFile delegates to that exact same function and only applies path.normalize, matching normalized filesystem/lease identity. The wrapper resolves once before acquiring locks, passes the absolute result to snapshots, then executes the native tool with original arguments. Literal ~ components, @ prefixes and file URLs therefore use the same native resolver; existing path-identity and journal cases passed on this candidate.
